newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat sees higher car output with incentives.
newsitem.headline: Fiat sees higher car output with incentives.

text.p: Italian car maker Fiat sees higher car production at its plants following the announcement of incentives early this year for motorists who trade in cars over 10-years old to buy new models.

"It is too early to make sales predictions, but orders are going well at the dealer level," said Fiat's managing director Paolo Cantarella while attending a conference organised by the Italian metalworkers employers association Federmeccanica.

Cantarella added that Fiat had drastically reduced its planned worker temporary layoffs for February, and had taken on new workers at its Melfi car plant. Both these were evidence of increasing car production.

Earlier this week, Fiat announced reduced worker layoffs for the four-week period of February 3-28, which will reduce production by 3,200 cars at its two Alfa Romeo plants in Pomigliano D'Arco, near Naples, and Arese northwest of Milan. In January, production cutbacks had been for 10,300 cars.
Fiat uses temporary layoffs, usually on a month-by-month basis, to align car output with demand.
The Melfi plant in southern Italy is Fiat's newest Italian car plant opened in January 1994 to produce the Fiat Punto small car and the similar-sized Lancia Y.
